newsitem.title: USA: Oakhurst completes H&H subsidiary sale.
newsitem.headline: Oakhurst completes H&H subsidiary sale.

text.p: Oakhurst Co Inc said Tuesday it completed the sale of its H&H Distributors subsidiary to its former vice president, James Stein.

The company said the deal included canceling debt owed by Oakhurst to H&H and transferring certain insurance claims to Oakhurst from H&H. The sale relieves Oakhurst of $900,000 in H&H leases and employment agreements.
Oakhurst on June 13 announced its intention to sell H&H. It said H&H incurred operating losses because of competitive pressures in its cellular telephone business and slow car accessories sales.
Earlier Tuesday, Oakhurst reported a loss of $315,000, or $0.10 a share, in the fiscal first quarter ended May 31, compared with a loss of $471,000, or $0.15 a share, in the year-earlier period.

The company attributed the improvement to the sale of Puma Products and H&H, which incurred a total of $40,000 in losses in the quarter ended May 31, 1996. It also cited a $60,000 reduction of goodwill amortization and the cutting of corporate overhead and interest expenses.
